At the less charged end, Fox News describes a "trans inclusion memo" as a reactive measure following male athletes' announcements, implying policy defensiveness without overt condemnation. The Federalist moves further, presenting an exclusionary tennis rule as self-evidently "Fair" and using the term "Men" rather than "trans women," a word choice that embeds a categorical claim within what reads as a neutral descriptor. At the most charged end, Breitbart's phrase "Stealing Women's Titles" applies explicitly criminal-adjacent language to a named athlete, and the addition of "Second Sport" constructs a narrative of escalating encroachment. The progression, then, is from institutional reaction framing toward increasingly adversarial and moralized language as scores rise.

stories.topicLabel: Jan. 6 legal cases, dismissals, and accountability debates
stories.analysis: Coverage of the January 6 legal cases was largely uniform across the outlets sampled, with a bias spread of just 1.0 point — a narrow range that reflects a broadly shared critical framing rather than meaningful ideological divergence. All three headlines leaned toward alarm or skepticism about accountability outcomes, differing mainly in emphasis. MSNBC took the most pointed institutional angle, declaring the system "did not hold" and that the cases "officially ended" with a dismissal — language implying systemic failure. The Star Tribune leaned on a former prosecutor's voice to characterize the present as a "unique, dire moment," framing a source sympathetic to prosecution as a credible alarm-raiser. HuffPost focused narrowly on Trump's rhetorical retreat, using the emotionally charged phrase "Furiously Backpedals" to describe his walk-back of a "vandalism" claim. No outlet in this sample offered neutral or procedurally detached framing; the shared register across all three was one of concern or criticism.

stories.topicLabel: Gender treatment for minors, hospital settlements, policies
stories.analysis: All three outlets covering this story sit on the center-right to right portion of the scale, producing a bias spread of only 1.5 points — meaning coverage was largely uniform in its skeptical-to-critical framing of gender treatments for minors, with differences being matters of degree rather than kind. The Free Press, at the lower end, used first-person "victim framing" through phrases like "Silenced My Views," centering a dissenting physician's perspective on institutional suppression. Breitbart escalated slightly by deploying non-clinical language — "Sex Change Drugs" rather than terms like hormone therapy — while framing DOJ enforcement approvingly. The Federalist, the most right-leaning outlet here, used the most charged language of the three, describing hospital conduct as "Years Of Serious Lies" and employing the pejorative, non-clinical phrase "Transing Kids." No outlet applied neutral clinical terminology or foregrounded the perspective of families or patients who supported the treatments.
